Janet (Acme): Hey team — after the March rollout our integration started getting different replies for previously stable prompts. Example: prompt: `Please extract agreement number from: \"Agreement # 12345 - Acme\"` used to return `12345` and now returns an empty string or a weird prefix. This started right after the 03/10 canary. Can we escalate?

sophie: Sorry you're hitting this, Janet. Can you paste a minimal curl request + model id you used? Also which environment (prod/dedicated/private)?

Janet (Acme): Using hosted API, model `redwood-std-001`, region us-west-2. Minimal repro: ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-std-001","input":"Please extract agreement number from: \"Agreement # 12345 - Acme\""}'
```
Returns: `"agreement_number": ""` or sometimes `"Agreement# 12345"` merged. Happening for a handful of customers after the rollout.

ashok: I pulled the canary diff. We deployed a tokenizer normalization change + a tiny chat-template tweak that strips leading/trailing zero-width spaces and collapses sequences of whitespace in system/user messages to a single space. Commit: `a7f4c2b` (tokenizer: normalize_unicode=True, collapse_ws=True).

ashok: Quick theory — the collapse_ws step merged the space between `Agreement` and `#` in some edge cases because the incoming content had a ZWSP (\u200B) between tokens from our input pipeline in older clients. The new normalizer removes the ZWSP and then collapses, changing token boundaries. Token boundary changes can change subsequent autoregressive decoding, esp. for patterns like `Agreement # 12345` which our few-shot extraction relied on.

devon: Confirmed the rollout window 03/10 02:14 UTC pushed that change to 5% canary -> we ramped to 50% then paused when ops started seeing anomalies. Canary status: `deploy-bot: canary 50% paused` (see below).

deploy-bot: Canary update: rollout a7f4c2b -> 50% (paused), health checks degraded on a small subset of text-extraction workloads.

ashok: Repro steps I used locally to show token delta:```
# inspect tokens before/after normalization (pseudocli)
redwood-tokenize --model redwood-std-001 "Agreement # 12345 - Acme" 
# before: ["Agreement"," ","#"," ","12345"," ","-"," ","Acme"]
# after normalization (collapse_ws+remove-zwsp): ["Agreement#"," ","12345"," ","-"," ","Acme"]
```
Changing the tokens led to the model preferring a different completion template (sometimes returning `Agreement# 12345` glued or returning nothing because the extraction pattern fell out of alignment).

marie: This explains customer reports. We need an immediate mitigation for customers on hosted API while we fix. Options: 1) revert the tokenizer normalizer in canary (rollback commit), 2) provide a prompt-level workaround (explicit separators), 3) instruct customers to pin to an older model variant (if available).
\sophie: Janet — short-term workaround: add an explicit separator in the prompt so extraction doesn't rely on token boundaries. Example: `Please extract agreement number from: \"Agreement — # — 12345 — Acme\"` or prepend a system message that normalizes input. That should avoid collapse ambiguity. Can you try and confirm?

Janet (Acme): Trying now... OK adding `—` helps, returns `12345` again. Not great to require prompt changes for many customers though.

ashok: For a quick patch we can change the normalizer to preserve ``#`` adjacency: skip collapse if `#` is adjacent to digits/punctuation. Patch snippet:```python
def collapse_ws_preserving_hash(s):
    # minimal: only collapse runs of whitespace that don't sit between letter/"#" patterns
    s = normalize_unicode(s)
    s = re.sub(r"(?<!#)\\s+|\\s+(?!#)", " ", s)
    return s
```
We'll add targeted unit tests around examples from support tickets.

devon: Plan: revert the broad collapse_ws on the canary (roll back a7f4c2b) to stop customer impact, then apply targeted patch and run regression suite. Rollback ETA 45m if no blockers.

marie: Support action items: 1) send Janet an official workaround + ETA and pin to customer ticket 48291; 2) offer temporary credits if they were significantly impacted.

ashot: (typo) ashok: Also adding an eval that runs our extraction prompt set through both normalizers to alert on token-boundary diffs in future deploys.

sophie: Follow-up question for engineering: do we have telemetry on how many customers' inputs include ZWSPs? Could be old SDKs or copy/paste flow.
\sashok: There's ~0.7% of extraction-labeled calls with any control/ZWSP chars, mostly from integrations that sanitize differently. I'll surface a dashboard tomorrow and link.

marie: Janet — we will: rollback canary -> pause ramp -> deploy targeted fix -> re-run canary with extra tests. ETA rollback 45m, patch + canary retest 4–6h. For now use `—` separation or let us pin you to pre-rollout variant. Would you like us to pin you?

Janet (Acme): Please pin us to pre-rollout variant, thanks. Really appreciate the quick responses. :pray:

sophie: Noted, opened internal ticket 48291 and a pin request for Janet's org. I'll keep this thread updated with rollback progress and the telemetry link when ashok posts it.

ashok: Posting follow-up once I have the token-diff dashboard. Also will commit the targeted normalizer test and block ramp until tests pass.

marie: Thanks team. Action summary pinned in ticket 48291: rollback -> targeted patch -> regression tests -> reroll.

Janet (Acme): Thanks everyone, will stand by.
